title: Getting started with Resgrid
summary: A new member's first course: your account, your status and staffing, responding to calls, and where messages, the calendar and training live.
overview: This course walks a new member through the parts of Resgrid they use every week. Adapt it to your department: add your own phone numbers, radio channels, station names and expectations before you publish it.

lessons.title: Signing in and your profile
lessons.html:
Your department invited you by email. Sign in on the web or in the Resgrid apps with the same account.

  • Check that your name, mobile number and email address are correct in your profile.
  • Choose how you want to be notified: push, text message, email or a phone call.
  • Turn on two-step sign-in if your department asks for it.

Your officers use your profile to reach you. Keep it current when your number or address changes.

lessons.title: The apps you will use
lessons.html:
Most members install the Resgrid responder app on their phone. It shows new calls, lets you respond, and sets your status and staffing with one tap.

Officers and dispatchers often also use the web application on a computer. Ask your training officer which apps your department expects you to install.

lessons.title: Setting your status
lessons.html:
Your status says what you are doing right now: for example responding, on scene or available. Set it as things change so that the people running the call see who is coming.

Your department may have custom statuses. Learn what each one means here before your first call.

lessons.title: Setting your staffing
lessons.html:
Your staffing says whether you can be counted on in the hours ahead: for example available, delayed or unavailable. Officers plan coverage from it.

  • Update it when you leave town or start a shift elsewhere.
  • Use scheduled staffing for regular commitments so you do not have to remember to change it.

lessons.title: Responding to a call
lessons.html:
When a call is dispatched you receive a notification with the call type, the address and notes. Open the call to see the map and the details.

  • Respond so that officers know you are coming.
  • Use the map or your navigation app to get there.
  • Read the call notes as they are updated on the way.

Never respond to a call you were not dispatched to unless your department's policy allows it.

lessons.title: Messages, the calendar and training
lessons.html:
Messages from your officers arrive in your Resgrid inbox and as notifications. The calendar shows drills, meetings and events you can sign up for.

Your assigned trainings and courses are under Training. Complete them by their due date; your transcript keeps the record of everything you finish.
